info.title: Azure Resource Graph Onboarding
info.description:
Azure Resource Graph onboarding control plane. Partners declare an offering, the ontology
(demand) they need, and the query endpoints that consume it; Azure Resource Graph resolves the
required publisher supply (data onboardings) and rolls the result out region by region.

put.description:
Creates an ontology or updates an existing one. Creating or updating an ontology re-runs gap
analysis against the supply currently available, and, when `autoOnboard` is set, materializes
data onboardings for every unmet type.

Gets an Azure region where an ontology has an activation record.
Lists the ontology activations in a single Azure region.
Gets the activation of an ontology in a single Azure region.

put.description:
Activates an ontology in a single Azure region, or updates an existing activation. Azure
Resource Manager routes the request to the Azure Resource Graph stamp that owns the region
named by the `locations` segment. A terminal provisioning state returns HTTP 200; a
nonterminal state returns HTTP 201. Control-plane completion does not imply completed
ingestion execution.

get.description: Lists the query endpoints in an offering.
Gets a query endpoint.

put.description:
Creates a query endpoint or updates an existing one. The ontology the endpoint references must
already be approved. This operation stores the consumer declaration; it does not provision a
query backend.

get.description: Lists the Azure regions where a query endpoint has activation records.
Gets an Azure region where a query endpoint has an activation record.
Lists the query endpoint activations in a single Azure region.
Gets the activation of a query endpoint in a single Azure region.

put.description:
Activates a query endpoint in a single Azure region, or updates an existing activation. Azure
Resource Manager routes the request to the Azure Resource Graph stamp that owns the region
named by the `locations` segment. The referenced ontology must be approved and have a
succeeded activation in this region. The operation stores the regional control-plane
record; it does not provision a query backend.

ActivationStatus.description:
Aggregate control-plane rollout state of a data onboarding, computed from its regional
activation children and its declared `targetRegions`. This does not indicate whether an
operator has completed ingestion execution.

This lives on supply only. An ontology is a blueprint with no physical footprint, so it carries
no activation state: its lifecycle is fully described by `provisioningState`, `reviewStatus` and
`validationStatus`. A query endpoint likewise reports where it is live through its own regional
activation children.

values.name: Pending
values.description: No regional rollout has started.

values.name: RollingOut
values.description: At least one target region has completed control-plane activation, but not all of them.

values.name: Active
values.description:
Every target region has completed control-plane activation. Regional execution is tracked
separately through `UnderExecution` and `Executed`.

DataOnboarding.description:
A data onboarding, the publisher-side supply record for the types an ontology demands. Partners
read these to discover which publisher covers a type they declared. Global ontology writes
generate unmet supply when `autoOnboard` is enabled; operators approve the generated records.
There is no public data-onboarding write operation.

properties.description: The resource-specific properties for this resource.

DataOnboardingActivation.description:
The activation of a data onboarding in a single Azure region. Azure Resource Graph materializes
one of these when an ontology is activated in the region, and operators advance it through the
review workflow as the supply is rolled out. There is exactly one activation per region, so the
resource is a singleton addressed by the fixed name `default`.

DataOnboardingProperties.description:
The properties of a data onboarding, the publisher-side supply record that covers one or more
node and edge types for a single provider namespace.

publisherNamespace.description:
The provider namespace that owns every entry in `types`, for example `microsoft.compute`.
Relationships use their own relationship type's namespace, not the source node's namespace.

types.description: Every node and edge type this publisher supplies.

targetRegions.description:
The regions this supply is intended to reach. This is the denominator for `activationStatus`:
the roll-up reports `Active` only once every declared region has a succeeded regional
activation. An empty list means no target set was declared, in which case `activationStatus`
reports `Active` as soon as any region succeeds.

ontologyRef.description:
The ARM resource identifier of the ontology whose declared types caused this data onboarding
to be created. Reusing covered types within the same offering does not overwrite this
provenance. Newly unmet types are grouped by publisher within each generation batch, so a
publisher namespace can have multiple onboarding records.

activatedRegions.description:
The regions that have completed control-plane activation, derived from the regional
activation children. This is the numerator to `targetRegions`, not an execution-readiness signal.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the data onboarding.

reviewStatus.description: The review lifecycle of the data onboarding.

activationStatus.description: The aggregate regional rollout state of the data onboarding.

rejectionReason.description: The reason the data onboarding was rejected.

EdgeOnboardingTypeSpec.description: An edge (relationship) type a data onboarding supplies.

relationshipType.description: The relationship type that connects the source and target node types.

sourceNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the source of the relationship.

targetNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the target of the relationship.

expectedEdgeCount.description: The total number of edges the publisher expects to supply.

EdgeTypeRef.description: An edge-type reference declared on an ontology.

relationshipType.description:
The fully qualified relationship type that connects the source and target node types.
Its own provider namespace identifies the publisher.

sourceNodeType.description: The source node's Azure resource type or its ontology-local alias.

targetNodeType.description: The target node's Azure resource type or its ontology-local alias.

IngestionEndpoint.description:
The ingestion endpoint resolved from the approved storage assignments during regional
control-plane activation. Its presence does not indicate completed ingestion execution.

uri.description: The URI the publisher sends notifications to.

supportedFormats.description: The notification payload formats the endpoint accepts.

NodeOnboardingTypeSpec.description: A node type a data onboarding supplies.

resourceType.description: The fully qualified Azure resource type, for example `microsoft.compute/virtualmachines`.

totalRowCount.description: The total number of rows the publisher expects to supply.

NodeTypeRef.description: A node-type reference declared on an ontology.

resourceType.description: The fully qualified Azure resource type, for example `microsoft.compute/virtualmachines`.

alias.description: An optional partner-facing alias for the node type.

Offering.description:
An offering, the global product boundary a partner onboards under. It owns the demand side
(ontologies and query endpoints) and the supply side (data onboardings).

OnboardingTypeSpec.description:
One type a data onboarding supplies, either a node type or an edge (relationship) type,
discriminated by `kind`. Nodes and edges share a single collection because a publisher onboards
both through the same pipeline and they are approved, provisioned and activated together.

Ontology.description:
An ontology, the data-model blueprint that declares the node and edge types a partner's scenario
needs. The definition is global; its per-region rollout lives on the activation children.

OntologyProperties.description:
The properties of an ontology, the data-model blueprint that declares the node and edge types a
partner needs.

displayName.description: The partner-facing display name of the ontology.

autoOnboard.description:
When `true`, creating or updating the ontology immediately materializes global data
onboardings for every unmet type. When `false`, gap analysis still runs and
`validationDetails` reports the gaps, but no new supply is created. Existing approved supply
can still satisfy the ontology; unmet demand keeps its derived `reviewStatus` at `Submitted`.

nodeTypeRefs.description: The node types the ontology declares.

edgeTypeRefs.description: The edge types the ontology declares.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the ontology.

reviewStatus.description:
The review lifecycle of the ontology. It is derived from the data onboardings referenced by
`validationDetails` and reaches `Approved` only once every one of them is approved. Regional
activation is blocked until then.

rejectionReason.description:
The rejection reason propagated from backing supply. Rejected supply leaves the ontology's
derived review status at `Submitted`.

approvedBy.description: The reviewer who last approved the ontology.

approvedAt.description: When the ontology was last approved.

rejectedBy.description: The reviewer who last rejected the ontology.

rejectedAt.description: When the ontology was last rejected.

validationStatus.description:
The aggregate availability of every type the ontology declares. It is the worst per-type
availability across `validationDetails`.

validationDetails.description: The per-type gap-analysis results for the ontology.

OntologySnapshot.description:
A point-in-time snapshot of an ontology's semantic body that a regional activation was
generated from. Only semantic fields are captured; read-only and cosmetic fields are excluded.

nodeTypeRefs.description: The node types declared by the ontology at snapshot time.

edgeTypeRefs.description: The edge types declared by the ontology at snapshot time.

OntologyStorageAssignment.description:
An operator-assigned physical storage placement for one ontology node or edge. Read-only on the
API surface: it is set when an operator approves the parent data onboarding and is copied onto
each regional activation so that a regional record is self-describing.

kind.description: Whether this assignment covers a node type or an edge type.

resourceType.description: The Azure resource type. Node assignments only.

relationshipType.description: The relationship type. Edge assignments only.

sourceNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the source of the relationship. Edge assignments only.

targetNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the target of the relationship. Edge assignments only.

scaleUnit.description: The scale unit the type is placed on.

dataset.description: The dataset the type is placed in.

logicalTableName.description: The logical table name the type is written to.

physicalTableName.description: The physical table name backing the logical table.

lookbackHours.description: How far back, in hours, the type's data is retained for reconciliation.

PeakNotificationRates.description: Peak per-minute notification rates for a node or edge type.

QueryEndpointProperties.description:
The properties of a query endpoint, a consumer activation request that references an approved
ontology within the same offering.

displayName.description: The partner-facing display name of the query endpoint.

ontologyRef.description:
The full Azure resource identifier of an approved ontology in the same subscription and
offering. The reference cannot be changed after creation. Legacy bare ontology names are
accepted on input and normalized; responses always contain the full resource identifier.

enginePreference.description: The preferred query backend. Omission records no preference and does not provision a backend.

estimatedQueriesPerDay.description: The expected daily query volume, used for capacity planning.

peakQueriesPerMinute.description: The expected peak query rate, in queries per minute.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the query endpoint.

QueryEnginePreference.description:
Preferred query backend recorded on an onboarding query endpoint. This preference does not
provision a query backend.

values.name: Galaxy
values.description: The Galaxy query backend.

values.name: Kusto
values.description: The Kusto query backend.

values.name: Pacific

values.name: NoPreference

RegionalActivationProperties.description:
The properties of a per-region activation. The same body is returned whether the activation
hangs off an ontology or off a data onboarding; the fields that do not apply to a given parent
are simply empty. `assignments` is populated only for a data-onboarding activation, and
`materializedDataOnboardingRefs` only for an ontology activation.

ontologySnapshot.description:
The snapshot of the ontology body this activation was generated from. When supplied on create
or update, Azure Resource Graph compares it against the currently approved global ontology and
rejects the activation if they differ, enforcing the one-active-rollout invariant. When
omitted, the drift check is skipped. It is persisted and returned on read.

region.description:
The Azure region this activation covers. It matches the `locations` segment of the resource
identifier.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the activation.

reviewStatus.description:
For data-onboarding activations, `UnderExecution` until the operator closes the region out
as `Executed`; approval happens globally on the supply record. The shared field is unused
for ontology activations and is returned with its default value, `Submitted`.

validationDetails.description: The per-type gap-analysis results for this region.

assignments.description:
The approved storage assignments this region has to execute, copied from the parent data
onboarding's approved configuration so that a regional record is self-describing. It is also
what a re-activation compares against to decide whether a region that already reported
`Executed` still is. Empty for an ontology activation.

ingestionEndpoint.description: The ingestion endpoint resolved for this region.

materializedDataOnboardingRefs.description:
ARM resource identifiers of the data onboardings materialized for this region as a side effect
of the activation. Empty when nothing was materialized.

items.description: A type definition that refers the id to an Azure Resource Manager resource.

ReviewStatus.description:
The onboarding review lifecycle. Advanced by Azure Resource Graph operators, never by the
partner. `Rejected` and `Executed` are terminal.

values.name: Submitted
values.description: The record has been submitted and is awaiting operator triage.

values.name: UnderReview
values.description: An operator is actively reviewing the record.

values.name: UnderExecution
values.description: The approved record is being rolled out.

values.name: Approved
values.description: The record is approved to execute.

values.name: Rejected
values.description: The record was rejected. Terminal.

values.name: Executed
values.description:
Rollout finished and the operator closed the region out. Terminal. Distinct from `Approved`,
which means "approved to execute" rather than "execution finished".

ValidationAvailability.description:
Per-type availability produced by ontology gap analysis, also used as the ontology-wide roll-up
in `validationStatus`. Declaration order is severity order — `Available` is best, `Unknown`
worst — and the roll-up is the worst value across every declared node and edge reference.

values.name: Available
values.description: Approved supply covers the type, or the platform catalog reports it as active.

values.name: OnboardingInProgress
values.description:
A data onboarding declares the type but has not been approved yet. This is the normal state
between a partner creating an ontology and an operator approving the resulting supply.

values.name: NotOnboarded
values.description:
Nothing supplies the type and the platform knows it is not onboarded: either the catalog
resolved it and reported no coverage, or, for relationships, no data onboarding declares it.

values.name: Unknown
values.description:
The platform cannot say. No data onboarding covers the type and the catalog has no entry for
it at all, so reporting `NotOnboarded` would assert more than is actually known.

ValidationDetail.description:
Per-type gap-analysis result. Carries the resolved data onboarding reference when the type is
(being) onboarded, which is how a partner discovers the supply record covering a type they
declared.

kind.description: Whether this detail describes a declared node type or edge type.

resourceType.description: The Azure resource type. Node entries only.

relationshipType.description: The relationship type. Edge entries only.

sourceNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the source of the relationship. Edge entries only.

targetNodeType.description: The Azure resource type at the target of the relationship. Edge entries only.

dataOnboardingRef.description: The ARM resource identifier of the data onboarding that covers this type.

reviewStatus.description:
The review status of the data onboarding named by `dataOnboardingRef`. The ontology's own
`reviewStatus` is a roll-up of these: it reads `Approved` only when every entry does, and
regional activation is rejected while any entry is still `Submitted`.

message.description:
A human-readable explanation of the availability result. Emitted only when `availability` is
not `Available`, that is, only when there is something to explain.

values.name: InternalOnly
values.description: Visible only to Microsoft-internal consumers.

values.name: PublicPreview
values.description: Available in public preview.

values.name: GA
values.description: Generally available.
